coverage.assessment: The main chain survives: act as though false, then the rams imply collusion, then the victory, then 'this is war', then the reply of 8 September, then the retrospect. The revision cut the 'old scores' and slow-British-mind setups that motivate the score-settling and the 'whole generation' quip. 'The notes' in para 8 lacks an antecedent; this is inherited and minor.

In the Milnes scene, the pronoun 'He' now misattaches to Adams. In para 13, 'Its' and 'They, too' have weak antecedents. The Portland Place location and the date sequence of 1, 3, 5 and 8 September remain clear.
The chapter has no live dialogue. The unspoken 'You come next!', the Minister's sentence, the secretary's imagined gloss, and Gladstone's quoted remarks are all correctly attributed and placed.

The draft keeps the hedges 'probably', 'as far as he ever knew' and 'or his biographer for him'. The gloss 'what no one else … doubted' inverts the source's 'felt any suspicion' and drops the reason, the legal-scope point. This is inherited from the first draft.

The 1889 biography is clearly marked as the later source, and the young secretary's certainty is set against the retrospect. The revision removed both 1863-present cues that Russell's 1862 intervention was then unknown.

The periodic sentences and the self-deflation survive in the key passages. The spring 1863 build-up is thinned to bare statements, losing the 'twenty-five years old' and 'at a cost that ruined' notes.

The reversal survives intact: the theory is proved wrong, 'he proved it', the education is rendered worthless, and the 'one or two' close follows. The contrast with Gladstone, and Russell as feeble but not dishonest, remains clear.
Both dependencies are intact. The Manchester leader is named locally and appears in 010.revision. The Gotha letter is referred to and is quoted in 012.revision.

strengths: All eight verbatim anchors survive. 'one or two' immediately precedes 'Earl Russell was certainly not one of the two.'
The secretary's three-point gloss is kept whole, so 'to complete the record' and 'The war was Russell's war' land.
The Bravay letter is paraphrased while keeping the comic 'easily settle that matter with the Turks.'
The 1889 biography is explicitly dated and set against the young secretary's 'idea of a boy'.
summary: The revision keeps the chapter's argumentative spine and nearly all verbatim anchors. These include Russell's mask, the vertigo of power, Milnes's embrace before Delane, 'this is war', the three-point gloss, the stopping of the rams, the 1889 biography's proof, the Bravay/Turks letter, and Gladstone's 'one or two' setup before the punchline. It is close to the 2,300-word target. One cut breaks the Delane scene: deleting 'Delane probably regarded it…' leaves 'He had never heard of young Adams' grammatically attached to Adams. Other revision cuts remove the 1863 limited-knowledge cues and the comic slow-British-mind setup. Two inherited referent and qualification slips remain in the retrospect.
